lessonRef.focus: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a 100° arc. Find it.

steps: Inscribed angle is half the arc.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 4, because the tangent bisects the radius
4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 30°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 41°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 164°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
